Our system reaches the same circuits from outside the head. A person sits in a chair, and within minutes focused ultrasound is acting on a target a few millimetres wide, deep in their brain. The target and dose are set in software, so we can act on a circuit, measure the response and adjust, session after session. company_description:
WorkProbe is an AI-native platform for hiring and staff training, built on three ideas:

1. Automatic work simulation. From a job description, WorkProbe builds a realistic 20 to 45 minute task. Candidates solve a real problem with documents, simulated colleagues and an AI assistant, and the team gets facts about what each one did, judged against must-haves it sets.
2. AI-first, adaptive steps. Each step adapts to what earlier ones found: pre-screening, CV analysis, simulation and final review.
3. One continuous data flow. A single data layer runs from job description to hire and is built to carry on into training, so nothing is lost between tools.

Companies use the full pipeline, single steps, or run WorkProbe on top of the ATS they already have. The same engine is being extended into staff training (L&D).

One paid pilot so far, with more sales and pilots under discussion. Top 100 Innovation at ARCTIC15 2026. US patent pending.

company_description:
Imii is a B2G platform that guides refugees through the resettlement and integration process while giving governments the tools to stop it from failing.

After status is granted, a refugee must secure housing, benefits, banking and documents in a strict order, across institutions that don't coordinate with each other. Missed steps end in homelessness and marginalisation, and European governments spend billions a year absorbing that failure.

Imii models the process as a dependency graph. The logic is data, not code, so one engine adapts to any city or country. Refugees get a personalised pathway in their own language, free of charge. Governments pay for caseload visibility, early warnings on stalled cases, and days saved in emergency accommodation.

The product is live and built in seven languages. Our first pilot with a London local authority is launching now. The UK is our beachhead; the model is scalable across EU.

company_description:
The Resourcly AI data platform was build to solve one specific problem: understanding what a part actually is, and connecting that across engineering, procurement, MRO and finance.

Our AI reads engineering files directly, 2D drawings, 3D CAD models and datasheets, rather than the records about them, because whether two parts are interchangeable lives in the geometry, tolerances, material and form factor, not in a text field. We hold that engineering truth and the commercial reality, stock, price and supplier, on one connected data layer, so every function works from the same part record.

We apply this across the entire existing portfolio and inventory, all part categories including MRO, not just new parts entering design, where the near term financial value sits. And we run continuously rather than as a project, keeping the parts layer current as portfolios change, with humans validating the decisions that matter, alongside existing ERP and PLM systems rather than replacing them.

company_description:

Electrifying process heat would require building out generation and grid on a scale nobody has committed to.

We deliver resilient and fossil-free process heat up to 1000°C without touching the grid. We concentrate sunlight & store it as heat in a thermal sandbattery. A patent-pending transfer device lets the sandbattery be charged directly with solar heat, so the chain stays thermal end to end. Most alternatives convert to electricity and back and lose 50–70% on the way. We don't, which gives us a much higher system efficiency & lower cost. 
Every MW that replaces natural gas mitigates 520t of CO₂e per year. The technology came out of Lund University. Our first paying pilot is signed with Orkla, starting this autumn.

company_description:
ferthe is a app that anchors art, culture and history in the places they came from. Artists, museums, podcasters and photographers place their work at the exact spot where it was made or where it happened, a photograph at the corner it was taken, a podcast episode at the site it describes. Users discover these spots by being there.

company_description:
Mechanical parking towers fill dense cities — 891,724 stalls in Korea alone — and almost none are connected. They run on closed PLCs from dozens of manufacturers, each with its own error codes, so a software fault still means sending a two-person crew across the city to press reset. Around 70% of call-outs are exactly that.

Gigto replaces that with software. Our edge controller speaks to any manufacturer's PLC and normalises it into one cloud API. Our platform gives operators remote control, unified error codes, predictive maintenance and per-stall analytics on a monthly subscription. Three maintenance companies run it on live sites today.

That same control layer unlocks what nobody else can: EV fast charging inside a parking tower. It is technically unsolved and, in Korea, illegal — no safety standard exists to certify against. We hold the only regulatory sandbox exemption, exclusive rights to 20 patents, a working 8-stall / 200 kW prototype, and an installation in Bangkok.

company_description:

company_description:
Soyle measures how much nitrogen a crop is actually carrying, field by field, from hyperspectral satellite imagery.

A farmer today has no direct way of knowing this. Nitrogen decisions are made from regional averages, soil tests taken weeks earlier, or rules of thumb; none of which tell you what the crop in front of you needs right now. So fertilizer goes on too heavily in some parts of a field and too lightly in others.

We retrieve canopy nitrogen by a physics-based radiative transfer model that describes how light interacts with leaves and canopies. Given the reflectance a satellite records, we solve backwards for the biochemical properties that must have produced it, protein and nitrogen content among them. The physics is the same everywhere, so the method needs no soil samples, no in-field hardware, and no per-farm calibration.

company_description:
Thistle builds the last-line air defence layer: the empty bottom of the air-defence stack, where cheap FPV drones now cause most frontline casualties and where firing a €1M missile at a €300 drone makes no sense.

We build it in three steps. The node — Thistle Shield, a 20 kg man-portable robotic weapon station that detects, tracks and engages a drone on its own optical and thermal sensors, driving weapons already in the unit's inventory, with a human authorising every shot. The cluster — nodes share tracks and split targets between them, so one drone is taken by one weapon and the sky never opens while another reloads. The layer — clusters join into one picture, take cueing from radar and tactical C2, and keep firing on their own sensors when the link is jammed.

A €300 drone is stopped with €2–18 of ammunition. The node is live-fire validated with a NATO member state's armed forces and pre-sold in Singapore; the networking is in development.

company_description:
Drug hunters lack causal immunology data. I&I discovery still leans on cell lines, mouse models and observational patient data, none of which show how a human immune system responds when you intervene. That is why targets look good on paper and fail in the clinic.

Graph is building the map we need to unlock better therapies at scale. The Functional Immune Manifold (FIM) is the most clinically relevant model for immune disease: a causal map of how primary immune cells from patients respond to perturbation across diseases, donors and immune states. We run the experiments ourselves and read out function, not just expression. AI steers every round toward the most novel and informative experiments.

This is data no one else has. We use it to find first-in-class, biomarker-backed targets for our pipeline and with pharma partners, and make FIM data and models available to partners who need to know which targets work in which patients.

company_description:
Grids and AI datacenters face ever more fast power swings: grid faults, frequency deviations, GPU load spikes. Handling them takes little energy but a lot of power, delivered instantly. Renewables are retiring the spinning machines that used to absorb these swings, while AI multiplies them. Geyser builds a power buffer for exactly this: supercapacitor-class cells that are water-based, non-flammable and made of low-cost, CRM-free materials. Making them needs no dry rooms or special fire protection, so factory capex is low.

A system-level prototype (768 cells, 440 V) was independently validated by Fraunhofer IEE in 2026. A Nordic hydropower operator has requested a proposal for a 100 kW pilot in 2027, and we are in technical engagement with a tier-1 grid OEM under NDA.

Butterfly Ventures, Voima Ventures, Tesi and the EIC Accelerator back us. Our team and board come from Skeleton and Maxwell. We are raising €5M to turn the prototype into a product with OEMs and customer pilots.

company_description:
Video is the last medium you cannot search. Text is queryable. Images are queryable. Video is still a file with a thumbnail on the front, and whatever is inside it stays invisible to the systems that need it.

Inphera is the intelligent data layer underneath. We index video at scene level, second by second, and turn what happens in the frame into structured data: objects, settings, people, brands, mood, sensitive content, each carrying a timecode. Four products run off that one index.

Discovery: describe a scene in your own words, get the timecode back.
Clearance: know the music at 00:14:40 is licensed only until 31 December, before the clip goes out.
Compliance: answer accessibility and youth protection questions about seconds, not a finished file.
Signals: target ads on what is actually in the frame.

Discovery and Clearance ship today, Compliance is on the roadmap. Our tagging still runs partly by hand, on purpose, because you cannot automate a judgement you have not made yourself

company_description:
Wodan protects trained AI models, so owners can run them on hardware they do not control without giving the model away.

A trained model is years of data, compute and expertise in one file. Once it runs on a partner’s site, a processor’s servers or devices, it can be copied. A contract cannot stop that.

Three layers protect it. Locked at rest: the model file is encrypted under a key bound to the device’s TPM (its hardware security chip), so a copy is useless elsewhere. Shielded while running: kernel-level shielding blocks attempts to inspect or tamper with it. Transformed inside: the weights are mathematically transformed, so a stolen copy never shows the real weights.

No loss of accuracy and 1 to 3% inference overhead, confirmed on your model and hardware in a pilot before you commit.

We are working with companies in food manufacturing, the automotive supply chain, power grid operation and the defence supply chain.

Your model IP stays yours. Deploy anywhere. Expose nothing.

company_description:
Guest OS is the regulatory data layer between an accommodation's PMS and the government. Every accommodation in Europe must register its guests and report them to national systems: the night register in the Netherlands, SES.Hospedajes in Spain, the fiche de police in France. Operators are personally liable for this, while privacy regulators forbid them to keep copies of ID documents. Existing check-in tools automate the form but leave the guest's data, and the liability, with the operator.

Guest OS is built to solve both at once. Our engine verifies the guest without storing a document image, applies the rules of each property's country and municipality, files the register on time with proof of filing, erases each record when its legal term ends and logs every step in an audit trail. The guest's personal data never reaches the operator, who only sees status. We run alongside the existing PMS and are onboarding pilot partners in the Netherlands and Spain.

company_description:
Optiqal solves the quantum incompatibility. Quantum computers, memories and sensors emit light at visible or near-infrared wavelengths; the world’s fiber network runs at 1550 nm. Without conversion, almost every photon is lost within a few kilometers; every quantum machine stays an island. Our quantum frequency converters translate the light of quantum hardware to telecom wavelengths and back, preserving the quantum state and entanglement – so distributed quantum computing and secure quantum links can run on the 5 billion km of fiber already installed.

Spun out of Saarland University, we have built converters for five qubit platforms – neutral atoms, trapped ions, diamond color centers and quantum dots; the closest competitor has demonstrated two. Our converters have carried entanglement over 33 km of telecom fiber. We ship them as 19-inch rack units: fiber in, fiber out, built to leave the lab. First paid order eight weeks after incorporation. We are preparing our pre-seed round now.

company_description:
EU medical device manufacturers must continuously monitor scientific literature and adverse-event databases for safety signals (EU MDR 2017/745). Today this is mostly manual: regulatory teams read hundreds of articles and judge one by one whether each describes a reportable incident. It is slow, expensive and hard to audit.

VigInfo automates this workflow. We ingest articles from PubMed, EBSCO and FDA MAUDE, use multi-pass LLM extraction to build a knowledge graph of individual events, devices and patients, and classify each event against EU MDR criteria with deterministic guardrails. Experts review and confirm results in our app, and every AI output and human decision is traced to its source text, so the audit trail regulators expect is produced automatically.

Unlike tools that classify whole articles, VigInfo classifies each event per device, so one article mentioning several devices or incidents is handled correctly.

company_description:
Okty shows you how your business actually runs, not how the documentation says it does.
Most companies have a small fraction of their processes both written down and current. The rest lives in people's heads or in systems nobody has mapped. So when they buy a new ERP, automate something, or start an AI project, they build on assumptions. That's where implementations overrun and automations underperform.

Okty starts by understanding the company itself: what it does, what each department is trying to achieve, which systems carry the work. Then it gathers evidence from three sources at once: your documentation, AI-led interviews with the people doing the work, and data from your systems. Than it reconciles them into one verified process map. Every step traces back to its evidence.

From there it surfaces the gaps, contradictions and workarounds, shows how each process translates into the system you're implementing, and ranks what to change by impact and effort.

company_description:
We're building an electrochemical engine to enhance grid resilience and reduce energy cost. 
The AV Cell Engine is an open thermodynamic device that draws net energy from the atmospheric thermal reservoir. An electrical input controls electron emission and transport; the output energy is sourced from the 
environmental gradient, not from the input. Oxygen participates as a reversible mediator (O₂ ↔ O₂⁻), localising where energy transfer occurs within the system without providing net chemical energy over a complete cycle. 

The process operates within established thermodynamic constraints, including Gibbs free energy and Carnot 
efficiency limits, with performance bounded by the available environmental gradients and system irreversibilities. We don't use any toxic chemicals, or rare earth metals.

We're working with Coca-Cola Europacific to reduce the electricity costs of their drinks cooler fleet. We're scaling our technology to halve the grid energy use of HVAC in data centres.

company_description:
Hyletic AI builds the world's richest training data for humanoid robots.

We record the full kinetic chain of human movement, fingertip to floor, together with the forces a camera can't see - pressure, shear and tear. Every channel runs on one clock.

Why it matters: humanoids learn physical skills from people, and most demonstration data shows only the motion. The robot is left guessing how firmly to grip, when a load starts to slip and how hard the feet must push to stay upright. That is where grips crush, objects drop and balance fails.

What we capture:
- Full-body joint motion full hand pressure, shear and slip.
- Audible validation
- Balance and ground reaction with foot pressure
- Object mass, shape and position

The body works as one system: grip tightening as a load shifts, the trunk bracing for a reach, the feet pushing back against the floor. Every episode is synchronised, calibrated and labelled.

company_description: Linro is a real-time cloud/infrastructure security platform. We evaluate every change to a cloud infrastructure at the control plane, the moment it is made, and block the harmful ones before they reach production. Cloud infrastructure no longer changes at human speed: engineers, CI/CD pipelines, and AI agents all hold credentials that can modify production. Posture management tools only scan what is already deployed and report what went wrong, so by the time the alert lands the public bucket exists and the over-privileged role is live. company_description:
Radical Dot turns local, mixed plastic waste into the molecules every industry runs on. Our first product is acetic acid, a building block for medicines, electronics and packaging. Europe’s last plant was mothballed in September, priced out by energy costs, so the continent now imports over 95% of its supply.

Our patented oxolysis process breaks plastic down with air at low temperature, with no external energy input, no hydrogen and no pre-sorting. That removes the three cost drivers (feedstock, energy, labour) that have kept plastic valorisation uneconomic, and puts our production cost below the imports Europe relies on. We start in a €25B market, with a path into a €250B one.

A fully automated, continuous pilot already runs on real post-consumer waste. We have €600k+ in paid projects with leading waste and chemical players and a €1.2B/year offtake pipeline. Our 200 kg/day demo plant, backed by a €3.88M federal grant, starts up in Q4 2027.

company_description:
Caplyzer is a KTH spinoff developing a patented, membrane-free electrolyzer for green hydrogen. Heavy industries like steel, ammonia and petrochemicals use 100 million tonnes of fossil hydrogen every year, emitting around a gigaton of CO2, and they cannot switch to batteries. Green hydrogen is the alternative, but today's electrolyzers produce hydrogen and oxygen at the same time. That requires costly membranes and creates gas-mixing risk and struggles with intermittent solar and wind.

Our supercapacitive electrolyzer works like a capacitor, producing hydrogen and oxygen at different times. This removes the membrane and the gas-mixing risk, and follows fluctuating renewable power directly. The result: safer, cheaper and flexible green hydrogen to decarbonize heavy industries.

We have a validated system prototype, a granted patent, are backed by prominent Swedish investors and are a passionate team with over 30+ years of experience in hydrogen, research and startups.

company_description:
Veterinary care is fundamentally reactive; silent chronic diseases are often caught too late. Routine blood screening is bottlenecked, because tests are bundled with full consultations, creating too expensive visits. Clinics are trapped in this structure to protect high-margin appointments, leaving preventive testing underutilized despite pet owners demanding human-grade care.
Abbis solves this by decoupling blood sampling from complex clinical exams through an asset-light marketplace. Pet owners book standardized, transparently priced biomarker tests online, visiting a partner clinic only for a short sampling appointment. Samples are routed to reference labs, and results are delivered digitally via our AI engine. For clinics, this eliminates the risk of cannibalizing major appointments. Instead, it monetizes open capacity, drives new foot traffic, and yields risk-free revenue via fixed sampling fees, while funneling newly patients back to them for high-value treatment.

company_description:
Farm Legacy is the first AI-powered platform for farm succession. We match retiring farmers with the next generation, run the full handover end to end (valuation, legal structuring, financing, EU grant applications), then provide the new farmer with the software they need to manage their farm operations, hiring, compliance, and grant applications.

In Europe alone, 6.3M+ farms need a successor in the next decade. Globally, 608M+ farms are aging without a clear plan for the next generation. When no one takes over, working farms get sold to industrial operators, absorbed into consolidation deals, or abandoned. The retiring farmer loses the value of their life's work, aspiring farmers without inherited land are locked out, and rural communities lose food production, biodiversity, and the family-scale farming that holds European agricultural ecosystems together.

We are building the platform that decides who farms next, starting in Finland and expanding globally.

We're already in paid pilots and active testing with professional AD studios and describers across Europe.

company_description: MOVIWA is an AI governance engine for regulated companies. It sits between employees and models such as ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini and does four things: detect, minimise, route and prove. Personal and confidential data is swapped for reversible tokens in 11 ms on the user's own device, so the AI never sees it and the answer is restored on the way back. A confidentiality router keeps sensitive work on a local model, and every decision leaves audit evidence mapped to GDPR, the EU AI Act, ENS and ISO 27001. The core is proprietary: compact models trained on NVIDIA H100 at MareNostrum 5 within the BSC AI Factory (EuroHPC), on Spanish legal and confidentiality corpora that don't exist publicly, scoring +14.4 F1 over the baseline and covering Spain's co-official languages. They run on CPU and on-premise. MOVIWA is sold as SaaS per user, deploys in minutes through a browser extension and is live in production with 3 paid pilots on real regulated data.

company_description:
Vulnerability research is a subdomain of cyber security, which concerns the process of reading code, or reverse engineering code of software in order to find security issues which can later be exploited.

If you look at vulnerability research as a problem to be solved, there are two phases to it. Discovery and exploitation.

Exploitation is a verifiable problem, as it requires you to write code in order to break into a system after discovering something. However, the former is usually not, the discovery process requires multiple bits of creativity, expert domain knowledge and many unquantifiable features.

Figuring out what causes these models to be good at vulnerability research and then training them specifically on different RL environments, methods of training, gathering data, etc. will require a lot of effort and experimentation. However, this is exactly what is needed.

We're working on RL envs, evaluation pipelines and models and training methods specifically for security.

We start with heating, plumbing and electrical trades in Rhineland-Palatinate, where our team is already inside the network.

company_description:
Heat is the leading cause of electronics failure, and in sealed systems it has nowhere to go. Data centers solved it with fans and liquid loops; defense radars, satellites and field electronics are sealed against vibration, dust and vacuum, and the seal traps the heat. Engineers design around it with less power, more metal and more space.

Thermaflux makes a solid, bonded graphite layer at millimeter thickness that routes heat out of the hotspot along a chosen path. It conducts heat about 4x better than copper and keeps 99.9% of it on route. On the bench, same heat, same size, same power: 43 °C cooler than copper. Cooler electronics mean more power, more life or less metal.

The company spun out of five years of research at the University of Twente, with the patent published in September 2026 and exclusively licensed. The first customer-paid pilot, in a radar transmit module, starts in Q4 2026. Radar first. Every sealed box after.

company_description: DYNANIC makes the part of a security or telecom system that inspects network traffic at full speed. Intrusion detection, DDoS protection, network monitoring and large telecom networks all have to look at every packet, and at 400 gigabits per second server processors can no longer do that economically. DYNANIC's unique architecture handles several packets in every clock cycle, so it scales to 400G and on to 800G by processing more in parallel, not by raising the clock frequency. It runs on standard FPGA cards from several manufacturers, and the customer controls everything from software. As threats and protocols change, new functions are added to cards in the field, so the hardware gains value over time instead of ageing out. Like ARM, DYNANIC licenses its IP rather than selling hardware: equipment vendors and operators build it into their own products and pay per card shipped and per function added, for as long as the product lives.

Cruxlens turns a business idea, plan or case into a structured strategic analysis. It doesn’t give opinions. It tests the claims behind the case: what holds, what doesn’t, where the real bottleneck is and which risks matter most.

We're building Orla to solve this. The idea is to give businesses a fallback system that runs on their own hardware, allowing their most important applications to keep working even when the cloud isn't available.

Unlike traditional backups, which help recover data after something goes wrong, we want to keep the actual software running.

We're starting with organisations where downtime is particularly costly, including critical infrastructure and other industries that can't afford to simply wait for their cloud provider to come back online.

company_description:
Plants emit ultrasonic sounds the human ear cannot hear, and those sounds change when a plant is under stress. Sonicflora builds the hardware and the AI that listen.

Capturing those signals inside a working greenhouse is the hard part: they are faint, the environment is noisy, and the hardware has to be cheap enough to cover a whole crop. We solve it with proprietary sensor design and inference at the edge, so each node decides what matters before anything is sent on.

What a grower gets is not a data stream but a direction: this section is running dry, adjust before the plants show it. In early trials the acoustic signal changes before symptoms are visible to the eye, and that lead time is what we are validating across crops now.

Every deployment adds labelled plant data from real production sites, which no competitor can buy. Agriculture today measures soil, air, climate and images. Sonicflora measures the plant itself.

company_description: Alzheimer's Disease is an unsolved healthcare burden for millions of patients worldwide and it overstretches the finances of every healthcare system. While there is still no complete scientific explanation for the origin of the disease, the leading hypothesis is the accumulation of multiple inflammatory protein types in patients' brains. All drug-approaches are monofactorial (clearing one type of toxic protein) and therefore have little effect on memory and quality of life preservation for patients. Healyan uses a sensory stimulation approach at gamma frequency (40Hz). THis method has shown promising results as a multifactorial, non-invasive therapy. Healyan maximizes adherence and efficacy by neuromodulating patients with a personalized system, in the form of glasses, while they go about their day. It is currently Europe's only company positioned to execute a phase 3 trial and gain MDR approval. After that, the system can be expanded into a therapy platform for other diseases.

company_description:
Enkryptify is a secrets management platform that automatically rotates, monitors and revokes the API keys, credentials, and environment variables that developer teams depend on.
Most tools focus on storing secrets securely and preventing leaks. We start from the opposite assumption: every credential eventually leaks, and a stolen key only causes harm because it still works. So instead of just locking secrets away, Enkryptify makes them worthless the moment they leave your control.
Secrets rotate on a schedule, automatically, across the providers teams already use. When a key leaks or starts behaving abnormally, it's revoked or rotated in seconds, without waiting for human approval. 
We're building toward ephemeral, scoped access for AI agents, the fastest-growing identity in the stack, where each key lives for seconds, not months. Built in Ghent, Europe.

The programme is moving from preclinical work into a Phase I clinical trial at the University Medical Center Mainz, supported by non-dilutive translational funding and protected by three patent families into the 2040s. We are a Rheinland-Pfalz biotech addressing a major unmet need in a multi-billion-euro market.

Our ambition is simple: make battery fire risk predictable, actionable and ultimately preventable — everywhere batteries are used.

Founded in Dortmund, ANT is scaling from first commercial deployments toward a European fleet.

company_description:
AI agents and MCP servers publish what each of their tools does, but nothing checks that it's true. Suncly runs an agent against its own tools, watches what actually happens, and issues a signed report showing where its behaviour matches its Agent Card or tool descriptions, and where it doesn't. Teams use our reports before submitting to the OpenAI and Claude app directories. One month in, we have paying customers, a tested company got into OpenAI's directory after acting on our findings, and we've had direct feedback from engineers behind Google's A2A protocol.

Where we're heading: continuous verification on every release, the neutral trust layer for the agent ecosystem. SOC 2 and app-store review, but for AI agents.

At Slush we're meeting investors for our €350k pre-seed round and teams building agents who want to pilot Suncly.

company_description:
Quantum Optima builds Optima Aegis, a decision-support module for counter-drone systems. When multiple drones approach at once, operators have seconds to decide which threats to prioritise and how to allocate limited defensive resources. Aegis computes an engagement plan within defined operational constraints, explains its recommendations, and lets operators review and approve them. In 100-run Monte Carlo simulations, it raised mission success from 33% to 59%.
Aegis is built to plug into existing command-and-control systems. We formulate the problem as a QUBO, so the same model runs on our classical solver today and is benchmarked on QAOA and quantum annealing via IBM Quantum and D-Wave, alongside, not instead of, the production solver. Aegis is at TRL 4; the same engine already runs in a paid energy-storage pilot. At Slush, we are raising our pre-seed and looking for European counter-drone and C2 integrators for joint simulation-based evaluation.

company_description:
Qraken Quantum develops hardware to enable long-distance quantum communication and the future quantum internet. Today’s cryptographic standards face obsolescence from emerging quantum computers, yet ground-based quantum communication is limited to ~200 km due to photon loss in optical fibers. Overcoming this requires quantum repeaters powered by quantum memories. 

We build high-performance quantum hardware based on our patented base technology: the Ultra-fast Quantum Optical Switch (UQOS). Combining ultra-low optical loss with ultra-fast switching, the UQOS enables our flagship Quantum Loop Memory (QLM). Unlike complex atomic memory systems, our all-optical approach preserves entanglement, stores multi-photon states noiselessly across broad telecom wavelengths, and integrates directly into existing fiber infrastructure. We manufacture and sell these core devices directly to quantum research institutions, tier-1 hardware OEMs, and telecom operators.

company_description:
Most people's cash earns nothing. £2.5trn sits in UK deposits, £523bn of it in current accounts paying 0.00%, because moving it is a chore nobody gets round to.

Riff is an autonomous savings agent. It connects to your accounts through open banking, works out what is spare against your spending, and moves the surplus to the best rate on our panel of partner banks. Your money never leaves your name - it is held on bare trust with you as beneficial owner and FSCS protection at the bank. You set the rules, the agent executes them.

Competitors optimise the rate. We optimise the rate and the amount.

The platform is two-sided. Savers get continuous optimisation, not a one-off switch. Partner banks get software to distribute live rates, build custom term products and bid for deposits in a daily interbank auction.

We are pre-launch. The FCA application is under review, our first panel bank is at contract stage, and the agent moves real money today. Revenue is 40bps of the interest.

company_description: Caen Hill Technology (CHT) is a Helsinki-based, seller-led trade credit platform. Large B2B sellers give their customers 70+ days to pay, which means they quietly run a lending book from their own balance sheet that nobody has ever priced. CHT gives them the evidence to shorten standard terms. When a deal genuinely needs longer terms, CHT makes that a priced exception: it assesses the buyer, checks the seller has room, then prices, invoices and writes the terms back into the seller’s ERP. CHT never lends and takes no credit risk. It earns fees, and the risk stays with the seller or, later, a bank or investor that buys the receivable.

company_description:
ForensifAI verifies image authenticity at the source. Every photo carries an invisible fingerprint left by the camera that captured it - we read it to confirm whether the image is genuine.

This matters wherever decisions depend on photographs: identity documents and passports, banking and KYC onboarding, insurance claims, journalism and news imagery, legal and forensic evidence. As AI-generated and manipulated images become harder to distinguish from real ones, most existing tools analyse content for signs of manipulation. We take a different approach: verifying the physical origin of the image itself.

Our approach was developed through a research collaboration commissioned by a European government authority, applying it to a real identity document pipeline. It is built on years of academic research in pattern recognition and digital forensics at the University of Groningen. ForensifAI's mission is to make image authenticity verification universally accessible.

company_description: Trince, winner of the 2024 Nature Spinoff Prize, is a Ghent University spin-off, founded in December 2021, focused on overcoming bottlenecks in intracellular delivery for drug discovery, high throughput screening, cell therapy, and advanced research. Its flagship product, the LumiPore™ platform, leverages proprietary photoporation technology—using laser-activated nanoparticles to gently and efficiently deliver a wide range of molecules into both adherent and suspension cells, including hard-to-transfect primary cells. Traditional intracellular delivery methods (viral vectors, electroporation, chemical reagents) are limited by cytotoxicity, poor scalability, and incompatibility with primary cells. The LumiPore platform addresses these challenges by enabling high-throughput, automatable, and gentle delivery with high cell viability and minimal impact on cell function. The platform is compatible with standard labware (up to 1536-well plates) and integrates easily into automated workflows.

company_description:
Zonova is addressing the critical global health challenge healthcare-associated infections (HAIs). HAIs affect 1 in 10 patients and are often caused by common medical devices like catheters, IV lines, and endotracheal tubes, which provide a surface for bacteria to grow and colonise. This leads to dangerous infections and complications such as sepsis and pneumonia which are becoming harder to treat as antibiotics lose their effectiveness due to antimicrobial resistance (AMR). The World Health Organisation predicts that AMR will cause 10 million deaths annually by 2050 and have an economic impact exceeding $100 trillion.

Our solution is a novel, patented antimicrobial technology that is embedded directly into these medical devices. This creates a protective surface that continuously kills a broad spectrum of pathogens on contact.

company_description:
AI is entering the physical world by storm. Yet, most AI agents work by trial and error: run a tool, check the result, undo, try again.  That works in software, where every step can be reverted. It doesn’t work in the physical world.  A valve opening, a load shifting or a line stopping can’t be rolled back. There is no "Ctrl+z”. 
Relayn OS is built for the physical world.
It decides as often as it needs to, and acts once. Before anything touches the real world, the intent is checked against the company’s rules, uncertain cases go back to a person, and every action is approved and logged. Rules decide, the LLM renders. It works with the systems a company already has, including legacy software with no modern API. Where no integration exists, Relayn OS works through the interface the way a person would. Add sensors, cameras, email and messengers, and it turns all of it into one picture of what’s happening and what needs attention.  It can run on your own hardware, with your own models.

company_description:
Valoron turns waste that nobody else can recycle into valuable fuels and chemicals, replacing fossil resources.

Supported by Breakthrough Energy, we are scaling our technology from the lab to industrial deployment.

company_description:
AI decisions increasingly span multiple organisations: the enterprise, outsourced processors, cloud platforms, models, agents and tools.

The problem is that accountability does not fragment with them. The enterprise still owns the decision, but the evidence needed to prove what happened is scattered across every trust boundary.

That is what PARCIS fixes.

We are building the independent decision evidence infrastructure for AI and autonomous systems: one common evidentiary spine across the whole decision.

PARCIS sits around the existing AI estate. At decision time it records what ran, which model and policy were active, which controls operated, who had authority, and what happened next. That record is cryptographically sealed and independently verifiable.

So when a regulator, auditor, customer or board asks, “prove what happened”, the organisation is not reconstructing the story from logs, emails and supplier portals.

The evidence already exists.

Capture once. Evidence many times.

company_description:
DNAMIC builds data storage that runs on DNA, for AI and cloud data centres.

AI is creating data faster than the world can store it. Data centres are running out of power, hard drives are sold out, and every few years all stored data must be copied onto new drives. So valuable data is deleted.

DNA is nature’s densest storage medium: one gram holds 200 petabytes, lasts thousands of years with zero energy, and is immune to power cuts, electromagnetic pulses and cyberattacks.

DNAMIC turns it into industrial storage. Our printer writes data into DNA with light, millions of strands at once, and our automated reader brings it back on demand. We start with the records no organisation can afford to lose, and grow into a storage tier inside every data centre as our cost falls, with AI and cloud as our biggest market.

Spun out of a €6 million EU research project, DNAMIC already has a first paying customer and seven letters of intent. We are ending the age of deleting.

company_description:
Every camera, sensor and medical scope has a hidden limit. Its optical filter only works when light arrives straight on. Tilt the light and the filter stops doing its job. Engineers have worked around this for decades with extra lenses, bigger housings and costly calibration.

We remove the limit. PoLightFilters is a University of Cologne spin-out that builds the world’s first angle-stable optical filters. Where conventional filters fail beyond 10 to 15 degrees, ours hold their performance up to 60 degrees.

That opens the door to smaller devices, fewer components and higher yield in production.

We start in endoscopy, where the filter sits directly on the sensor at the tip of the instrument and the angles are largest. From there, the same filter serves any imaging and sensing system limited by the angle of light.

The physics works in the lab. Now we build the product.

company_description:

Models run on-prem, in private cloud or air-gapped, so no customer data leaves the institution. Every decision comes with a full reasoning trace, and model cards, risk registers and conformity documentation are generated automatically for the EU AI Act, GDPR and AML/KYC.

We started in lending, with headless origination, servicing and onboarding live at banks including OTP and ProCredit, and cost per loan application cut from $2,000 to $200. Next, we’re bringing deterministic control to every BFSI workflow, including AI agents.

company_description:
Deepentix is the fastest path to auditable AI for regulated enterprises,(i.e. pharma, insurance, compliance) where a hallucinated answer is a legal, financial or clinical liability.

Generic LLMs and chunk-based RAG collapse on multi-tier documents: EU regulations, national rules, corporate policy, branch overrides, and the contract in hand. Peer-reviewed work shows up to 100% failure on specific dose formulation; the EU AI Act makes traceability a binding duty for high-risk AI by December 2027, with fines up to €35M or 7% of global turnover.

Our engine turns enterprise documents into an auditable Claim Graph, populated by domain-specialized Small Language Models running inside the customer's own cloud or on-prem. Every claim carries its qualifiers, constraints, confidence, and full source path.

Result: SOTA accuracy at 38% fewer tokens on public multi-hop benchmarks, 15–40× cheaper extraction than frontier APIs, new use cases rolled out in 1 day, zero data egress.

company_description:
Enterprises are pouring trillions into AI and getting copilots back. That is a trust problem, not a technology one: nobody lets an agent act where a mistake gets them fined or sued.

Coalex is the Decision Firewall, the European trust layer for regulated AI agents. Every agentic action is checked in real time against two questions: is it safe (the agent is competent and uncompromised) and is it right (it complies with company policy, DORA and the EU AI Act). Safe actions clear instantly; risky ones are blocked before they execute, routed to the right human, and logged as a defensible audit trail. Observability tells you an agent already did something it shouldn't; we stop it in the path. Every human decision trains the system to auto-approve more, so oversight cost falls while a live Health Score per agent lets customers prove their AI is safe.

We are in paid production across four regulated sectors in the EU and Brazil.

company_description:
Electrification is pushing demand up faster than grids can expand. Yet much of the capacity in batteries, solar and building systems sits underused because it cannot respond to changing prices and demand.

Neura Energy gives large commercial and industrial buildings an intelligent operating layer. Batteries, solar and cooling systems predict, adapt and optimise in real time, so sites get more from what they already have.

ThermaFlex optimises chiller plants, one of the biggest loads on site. It shifts cooling to cheaper hours and runs equipment more efficiently, so sites save twice: fewer kWh and cheaper kWh. Comfort is kept and no new chillers are needed.

NeuraFlex manages batteries and solar. It lets sites run more load than their grid connection allows, so they can expand or electrify without waiting for a grid upgrade. It also times charging to cut peak costs.

The result is more capacity from existing infrastructure, helping electrification move faster.

company_description:
Up to half of endurance athletes are injured every year, mostly through overuse. It happens despite Garmin and Whoop, because none of them measures the thing that fails. Every wearable is built on heart rate, the easiest signal to capture, not the right one.

Existing LoL tools show win rates: how often players who made a choice then won. Coachless shows win probability added (WPA): how much a choice, given the game state at that moment, moved the odds of winning. The method comes from CEO Perttu Jalovaara's Aalto thesis "Win probability estimation for strategic decision making in esports" (2024), supervised by CTO Oliver Struckmeier, on deep learning models they built together.

company_description:
Lorasis builds a cybersecurity Trust Operating System that gives every workload, agent, and AI inference a hardware rooted proof of integrity, not just a promise of it. company_description:
TentrisDB is a new RDF graph database built for Enterprise AI and large-scale knowledge graphs. Its novel storage architecture and worst-case optimal multi-way joins enable complex graph analytics with significantly lower memory requirements than traditional graph databases. This allows organizations to process larger knowledge graphs, reduce infrastructure costs and unlock AI applications based on highly connected data.

Building on TentrisDB, we are developing neuro-symbolic World Models (WOLFs) that combine scalable knowledge storage with neural representations and formally verifiable reasoning. WOLFs provide AI agents with persistent memory, reasoning and verification, enabling them to access explicit world knowledge, reason across complex relationships and generate understandable justifications.

Our vision is to build the semantic backbone for Enterprise AI: trustworthy, connected and explainable knowledge that powers the next generation of AI agents.

company_description:
Everything you know about the people in your life is scattered, and it decays. It's in your head, in old texts, in a note somewhere, and the moment you need it, it's gone.

Deeta is the layer where it lives: structured, AI queryable in plain language, encrypted on your device. Private and secure by architecture rather than policy.

Capture is frictionless: dictate, paste, or save from email, iMessage or any app. Every prior attempt asked you to maintain the record by hand, so it rotted and people stopped opening it. Deeta inverts that. The contact maintains their own side, so when someone updates any detail it automatically updates on yours. The record doesn't decay, it improves as more people join and add detail.

It's also the relationship memory AI agents lack. They read your calendar but have no idea your sister is vegan. We serve that through a patent-pending zero-knowledge endpoint where your own device answers, so we hold no readable copy and no key.

iOS launches 29 September.

The University of Glasgow has been changing the world since 1451, tackling the world’s challenges through creativity, innovation and partnership. 

We have nurtured Nobel laureates and prime ministers, inventors and renowned thinkers, award-winning writers and human rights activists, as they’ve sought to push forward the boundaries of what’s possible.
